subtitle: Cross-check of 09/Oct/2026, fifth day of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): Polymarket at the confirmed reading of 09/Oct, 14:06 BRT, the post-vote national polls from AtlasIntel/Bloomberg and Vox Brasil of 09/Oct and from Datafolha and PoderData/Aya of 08/Oct, the official [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) final tally and the press flow of 08 and 09/Oct.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: PRICE: 13.50% (vol USD 21.20M cumulative) in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 09/Oct, 14:06 BRT, holds steady against the confirmed reading of 08/Oct at 20:38 BRT, published in the previous update. COUNT: 45.16% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). POLL: 44.2% to 42.7% in Vox Brasil and 45.7% to 51.1% in AtlasIntel, both of 09/Oct.
fortes: He leads Vox Brasil of 09/Oct by 44.2% to 42.7%, within the margin of 2.15 points, and has 50.86% of the valid votes.
In AtlasIntel of 09/Oct, 50.4% of Augusto Cury's voters vote for him and 38.9% for Flávio Bolsonaro, even with Cury's declared support for his rival on 08/Oct.
🏆 Counting the closed contracts, his contract is still the one with the highest cumulative volume in the presidential book, USD 21.20M.
fracos: He stands at 13.50% in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 09/Oct, 14:06 BRT, and Flávio Bolsonaro's gap over him is 73.65pp.

He trails in three of the four national polls conducted after the vote: 45.7% to 51.1% in AtlasIntel of 09/Oct, 45% to 49% in Datafolha and 44% to 49% in PoderData/Aya of 08/Oct; in Datafolha, 46% say they would not vote for him.
He finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) 1.87 points behind Flávio Bolsonaro, with 45.16% of the valid votes against 47.03%.
In [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 03/Oct government approval went from 46% to 44%, with 49% disapproval.
candidates.analise: Lula stands at 13.50% in the winner contract (vol USD 21.20M cumulative), confirmed reading of 09/Oct, 14:06 BRT, and holds steady against the confirmed reading of 08/Oct at 20:38 BRT, published in the previous update. 🗳️ He had 45.16% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). 📊 In Vox Brasil of 09/Oct he has 44.2% against 42.7%, the first national poll after the vote with him ahead, and in AtlasIntel of the same day he has 45.7% against 51.1%; on 08/Oct he had 45% in Datafolha and 44% in PoderData/Aya. On 09/Oct Lula held the first campaign event of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), defending the end of the 6x1 work schedule, six days on and one off (Estadão and Folha de S.Paulo), and indicated that he will attend the debates (O Globo). ⚖️ The [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) ordered his campaign and first lady Janja to take down videos about cuts to social programs in a possible Flávio Bolsonaro government (Agência Brasil and Folha de S.Paulo). ⛔ The panel does not attribute the price to the polls or to the schedule: it measures the sides with each one's timestamp.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: PRICE: 87.15% (vol USD 18.88M cumulative) in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 09/Oct, 14:06 BRT, up 1.50pp against the confirmed reading of 08/Oct at 20:38 BRT, published in the previous update. COUNT: 47.03% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). POLL: 51.1% to 45.7% in AtlasIntel and 42.7% to 44.2% in Vox Brasil, both of 09/Oct.
fortes: He finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) ahead, with 47.03% of the valid votes against Lula's 45.16%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally.
He stands at 87.15% in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 09/Oct, 14:06 BRT.

He leads three of the four national polls conducted after the vote: 51.1% to 45.7% in AtlasIntel of 09/Oct, 49% to 45% in Datafolha and 49% to 44% in PoderData/Aya of 08/Oct (Estadão, G1 and Jovem Pan).
He has the declared support of Podemos, Augusto Cury, Novo, ACM Neto, PP, União Brasil, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema and Michel Temer.
Among Ronaldo Caiado's voters, he has 54.9% against 26.9% in AtlasIntel of 09/Oct and 57% against 19% in PoderData/Aya of 08/Oct.
fracos: He trails in Vox Brasil of 09/Oct, with 42.7% against 44.2%, within the margin, and in Datafolha of 08/Oct 43% say they would not vote for him.

🏦 According to O Globo, the [Federal Police](/en/glossary#pf) is investigating, in the inquiry into Daniel Vorcaro and Master's relationship with BRB, the bank's R$ 3.1 million financing to Flávio Bolsonaro for the purchase of a R$ 6 million mansion in Brasília; he says the transaction was legal, and the report comes from a single media group and is included here with attribution.

📰 Messages extracted from Daniel Vorcaro's phone and published by Estadão on 24/Sep show four attempts by him to contact the banker between 13 and 16 November 2025, in the days before Vorcaro's arrest, on 17 November 2025. Gazeta do Povo confirmed the authenticity of the exchanges with its own sources close to the investigation.
candidates.analise: Flávio Bolsonaro stands at 87.15% in the winner contract (vol USD 18.88M cumulative), confirmed reading of 09/Oct, 14:06 BRT, and rises 1.50pp against the confirmed reading of 08/Oct at 20:38 BRT, published in the previous update. 🗳️ He had 47.03% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). 📊 Two national polls came out on 09/Oct. In AtlasIntel/Bloomberg, with online fieldwork from 03 to 08/Oct and 5,026 interviews, Flávio Bolsonaro has 51.1% and Lula 45.7% in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), with 3.2% blank ballots, spoiled ballots and undecided voters; in valid votes, 52.8% to 47.2% (Estadão, CNN Brasil and CartaCapital). In Vox Brasil, with in-person fieldwork from 05 to 07/Oct and 2,100 interviews, Lula has 44.2% and Flávio Bolsonaro 42.7%, within the margin, with 3.4% blank and spoiled ballots and 9.7% who do not know; in valid votes, Lula gets 50.86% of the votes and Flávio Bolsonaro 49.14% of the votes (CartaCapital, CNN Brasil and Poder360). On 08/Oct, Datafolha gave Flávio Bolsonaro 49% to 45% and PoderData/Aya 49% to 44% in the total vote. 🤝 Flávio Bolsonaro has the declared support of Podemos and Augusto Cury, since 08/Oct, and of Novo, ACM Neto, PP, União Brasil, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema and Michel Temer; PSDB stayed neutral and released its members (Congresso em Foco and CartaCapital). Lula has the support of UP, PSTU and PCB (CNN Brasil and G1), and Renan Santos still backs no one (CNN Brasil and Estadão). 📺 With the return of free electoral airtime, on 09/Oct, Flávio Bolsonaro promised to keep the social programs and spoke of change, and Lula warned of a setback and criticized cuts made by the Jair Bolsonaro government (G1, Folha de S.Paulo and O Globo). ⚖️ In individual (single-judge) rulings published on 09/Oct, the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) president, Kassio Nunes Marques, ordered the removal of a video by first lady Janja that said Flávio Bolsonaro would end Farmácia Popular, and the vice president, André Mendonça, ordered Lula's campaign to take down videos linking the R$ 200 billion cut proposed by Flávio Bolsonaro to losses in social programs. Both wrote that these claims lack a minimum factual basis, and the rulings still go to the TSE full court (Agência Brasil and Folha de S.Paulo). ⛔ The panel does not attribute the price to the polls or to the endorsements: it measures the sides with each one's timestamp.

candidates.name: Augusto Cury
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): third place, with 2.89% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. PRICE: winner contract closed and resolved at zero, with USD 5.51M cumulative. [SECOND ROUND](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro on 08/Oct (G1, Estadão and CNN Brasil).
fortes: He finished third, with 2.89% of the valid votes, ahead of Renan Santos and Ronaldo Caiado.
The [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno)'s third-place book was resolved in his favour.
fracos: He is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and his contract in the winner book was resolved at zero.
On the eve the third-place book paid more for Renan Santos, 47.50%, and for Ronaldo Caiado, 30.00%, than for him, 23.70%.
candidates.analise: Augusto Cury finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in third, with 2.89% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally, and is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). His contract in the winner book was closed by Polymarket after the first round and resolved at zero, with USD 5.51M cumulative. The first round's third-place book, which on the eve paid 23.70% for him, at 23:00 UTC on 03/Oct, was resolved in his favour. 🤝 On 08/Oct he declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in the second round (G1, Estadão and CNN Brasil).

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): fourth place, with 2.24% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. PRICE: winner contract closed and resolved at zero, with USD 17.12M cumulative. [SECOND ROUND](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): he backs neither of the two.
fortes: He finished fourth, with 2.24% of the valid votes, ahead of Ronaldo Caiado, with 2.18%.
His contract in the winner book closed with USD 17.12M cumulative, the second largest in the presidential book.
fracos: He is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and his contract in the winner book was resolved at zero.
On the eve the third-place book paid 47.50% for him, and third place went to Augusto Cury.
candidates.analise: Renan Santos finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in fourth, with 2.24% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally, and is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). His contract in the winner book was closed by Polymarket after the first round and resolved at zero, with USD 17.12M cumulative, the second largest in the presidential book, behind Lula's. On the eve the third-place book paid 47.50% for him, at 23:00 UTC on 03/Oct, and it was resolved in favour of Augusto Cury. 🤝 On the night of 04/Oct he said he backs neither of the two in the second round and freed Missão's activists to choose (Gazeta do Povo and Agência Brasil).

candidates.name: Caiado / Haddad / Zema
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): Ronaldo Caiado, with 2.18% of the valid votes, and Romeu Zema, with 0.27%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. Fernando Haddad did not run for President. PRICE: the three winner contracts were closed and resolved at zero.
candidates.subtitle: The three names outside the leading pack, with the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) final tally (100% of polling sections) and the closing of the winner contracts after the first round.

caiado.label: CAIADO (PSD), eliminated in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) with 2.18% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.82M cumulative.
caiado.fortes: He declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in Goiânia on 06/Oct, with governor Daniel Vilela (O Globo and VEJA).
caiado.fracos: He finished fifth, behind Renan Santos, and the PSD decided on neutrality in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (Folha de S.Paulo and Agência Brasil).

haddad.label: HADDAD (PT), did not run for President: he ran for governor of São Paulo and lost to Tarcísio de Freitas in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.74M cumulative.
haddad.fortes: The top of his series in the winner contract was 7.60%, on 26/May, measured in the database backup.
haddad.fracos: He was not measured by any national poll in a presidential scenario or in a second-round pairing.

zema.label: ZEMA (Novo), eliminated in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) with 0.27% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.74M cumulative.
zema.fortes: ⭐ In [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 28/Sep, 81% of his voters would go to Flávio Bolsonaro in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), the largest transfer among the names measured (O Globo).
zema.fracos: He had 0.27% of the valid votes. He declared his vote for Flávio Bolsonaro on 05/Oct, and Novo declared support for him on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital).

candidates.analise: 🗳️ Ronaldo Caiado finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in fifth, with 2.18% of the valid votes, and Romeu Zema had 0.27%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. Fernando Haddad ran for governor of São Paulo, not for President. The three contracts in the winner book were closed by Polymarket and resolved at zero. 🤝 Romeu Zema declared his vote for Flávio Bolsonaro on the night of 05/Oct (G1 and Folha de S.Paulo), and Novo, his party, declared support on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital). Ronaldo Caiado declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in Goiânia on 06/Oct (O Globo and VEJA), even with the PSD neutral in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (Folha de S.Paulo and Agência Brasil).
fortes: Ronaldo Caiado declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro on 06/Oct (O Globo and VEJA), and Romeu Zema declared his vote for him on 05/Oct, followed by Novo on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital).
⭐ In [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 28/Sep, 81% of Romeu Zema's voters and 42% of Ronaldo Caiado's would go to Flávio Bolsonaro in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (O Globo).
fracos: The two are out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and the winner contracts of all three names were resolved at zero.
Fernando Haddad did not run for President: he ran for governor of São Paulo and lost to Tarcísio de Freitas in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno).

cruzamento: Fifth day of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), with four national polls conducted after the vote. 💹 In the confirmed reading of 09/Oct, 14:06 BRT, Flávio Bolsonaro rises 1.50pp and Lula holds steady against the confirmed reading of 08/Oct at 20:38 BRT, published in the previous update, and the gap goes from 72.15pp to 73.65pp. 📊 Two national polls came out on 09/Oct. In AtlasIntel/Bloomberg, with online fieldwork from 03 to 08/Oct and 5,026 interviews, Flávio Bolsonaro has 51.1% and Lula 45.7% in the second round, with 3.2% blank ballots, spoiled ballots and undecided voters; in valid votes, 52.8% to 47.2% (Estadão, CNN Brasil and CartaCapital). In Vox Brasil, with in-person fieldwork from 05 to 07/Oct and 2,100 interviews, Lula has 44.2% and Flávio Bolsonaro 42.7%, within the margin, with 3.4% blank and spoiled ballots and 9.7% who do not know; in valid votes, Lula gets 50.86% of the votes and Flávio Bolsonaro 49.14% of the votes (CartaCapital, CNN Brasil and Poder360). On 08/Oct, Datafolha gave Flávio Bolsonaro 49% to 45% and PoderData/Aya 49% to 44% in the total vote. In the two pollsters' rounds conducted before the vote, AtlasIntel of 03/Oct had Lula at 47.6% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 47.4%, and Vox Brasil of 02/Oct had Flávio Bolsonaro at 48.2% and Lula at 45.2%. Augusto Cury's voters split in opposite directions in the two measurements: in AtlasIntel of 09/Oct, 50.4% of them vote for Lula and 38.9% for Flávio Bolsonaro; in PoderData/Aya of 08/Oct, 56% vote for Flávio Bolsonaro and 27% for Lula (Jovem Pan). Among Ronaldo Caiado's voters both point to Flávio Bolsonaro, 54.9% to 26.9% in AtlasIntel and 57% to 19% in PoderData/Aya. 🤝 Flávio Bolsonaro has the declared support of Podemos and Augusto Cury, since 08/Oct, and of Novo, ACM Neto, PP, União Brasil, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema and Michel Temer; PSDB stayed neutral and released its members (Congresso em Foco and CartaCapital). Lula has the support of UP, PSTU and PCB (CNN Brasil and G1), and Renan Santos still backs no one (CNN Brasil and Estadão). ⚖️ In individual (single-judge) rulings published on 09/Oct, the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) president, Kassio Nunes Marques, ordered the removal of a video by first lady Janja that said Flávio Bolsonaro would end Farmácia Popular, and the vice president, André Mendonça, ordered Lula's campaign to take down videos linking the R$ 200 billion cut proposed by Flávio Bolsonaro to losses in social programs. Both wrote that these claims lack a minimum factual basis, and the rulings still go to the TSE full court (Agência Brasil and Folha de S.Paulo). 📊 The next national polls registered with the TSE come out on 10/Oct (Ipespe), 11/Oct (DataTrends), 13/Oct (PoderData, Gerp, Nexus and 100 Cidades) and 14/Oct ([Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest)). 📌 Correction: on 08/Oct this panel said that PoderData/Aya had published only valid votes. It also published the total, 49% for Flávio Bolsonaro and 44% for Lula, with 5% blank and spoiled ballots and 2% undecided (Jovem Pan), and the total was added to its entry. By the chart's rule, the source for 08/Oct would have been PoderData/Aya, with the larger sample, and not Datafolha: Flávio Bolsonaro's number is the same, 49%, and Lula's is 1 point lower, 44% instead of 45%. ⛔ The panel does not attribute price moves to the polls, to the endorsements or to the day's acts: it measures the sides with each one's timestamps.
